body.heading: Wonder out loud
paragraphs: Find a clean empty jar. Every time you wonder about something this week, say it out loud: “Why is the sky blue?” “Where do ants sleep?”
Your adult writes each question on a slip of paper and drops it in the jar. No question is too small or too strange.

body.heading: Pick one together
paragraphs: Once a week, tip the jar out and pick one question together. Talk about what you already think the answer might be.
Some questions have answers you can test, like whether ice melts faster in the sun or the shade. Some are just wonderful to think about.

body.heading: Wondering is the point
paragraphs: You do not have to answer every question. Wondering is a skill, and scientists practise it their whole lives.
When the jar gets full, celebrate. A full wonder jar means your curiosity has been working hard.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: collect your biggest and smallest wonderings in a jar and explore one each week.
